{"consent_letter_en": "[DATE]

To: [LANDLORD/PROPERTY MANAGER]
Re: Request for written consent to sublet [PREMISES ADDRESS]

Dear [LANDLORD/PROPERTY MANAGER],

I am Alex Kim, a resident under the lease for the premises. Under the lease’s subletting provision (p. 1), I request your prior written consent for Jordan Rivera to occupy the premises from June 1, 2027 through July 28, 2027, at a sublease rent of $1,950 per month, with a $1,500 security deposit held in Rentrail escrow until the return inspection.

Please confirm in writing whether you approve this sublet and identify any required approval documents. The lease states that a $150 administrative fee applies if consent is granted (p. 1). Please advise how and when to pay it. I understand that I and any remaining residents continue to be responsible for the lease obligations, including damage caused by a subtenant (p. 1).

This request does not seek to change or extend the master lease. Please also confirm any move-in procedures that Jordan Rivera must complete, including proof of the required liability insurance (p. 6).

Sincerely,

Alex Kim
[PHONE/EMAIL]", "agreement_md_en": "# Sublease Agreement (Draft — Subject to Landlord’s Written Consent)

**Do not sign or allow occupancy until the landlord gives prior written consent.** The master lease requires written consent for a sublet (p. 1).

## 1. Parties and premises
- **Sublessor:** Alex Kim
- **Subtenant:** Jordan Rivera
- **Premises:** [PREMISES ADDRESS]
- **Master landlord/property manager:** [LANDLORD/PROPERTY MANAGER]
- **Master lease:** Lease running August 1, 2026 through July 31, 2027.

## 2. Term and rent
The sublease term is **June 1, 2027 through July 28, 2027**, subject to written landlord consent. Rent is **$1,950 per month**. Before signing, the parties must put in writing the exact payment dates and any prorated amount for the partial July period; no prorated amount is assumed in this draft. The master lease requires rent to be paid in advance through the resident portal by the first of the month and does not accept cash (p. 1). The parties must confirm the permitted payment method and avoid any arrangement that conflicts with the master lease.

## 3. Security deposit and escrow
The subtenant will pay a **$1,500 security deposit** to **Rentrail escrow**, to be held until the return inspection. Before accepting the funds, the parties must confirm that the escrow arrangement satisfies Connecticut’s requirement that a landlord deposit the full security deposit in an escrow account at a financial institution (CT-47a-21-h1). The sublessor, as a tenant who sublets, is a landlord for deposit purposes (CT-47a-21-a7).

The sublessor will provide the required written notice identifying the amount held and the financial institution’s name and address within 30 days after receiving the deposit (CT-47a-21-h4). The sublessor will return the deposit balance and applicable accrued interest, with a written itemized statement for any lawful deductions, no later than **August 18, 2027**, unless the statutory forwarding-address rule makes a later date applicable (CT-47a-21-d2; CT-47a-21-i). Any claimed deduction must be for an actual, supportable loss and itemized; ordinary wear and tear is not a damage deduction. The parties will not charge for pre-existing conditions. Any deposit use must be limited to legally permitted obligations and documented amounts (CT-47a-21-a14; CT-47a-21-d2; DOB-itemize).

## 4. Utilities and services
- **Electricity:** The subtenant is responsible during the sublease term and must arrange the account before move-in if the utility provider permits. The master lease says residents open an account with Shoreline Electric (p. 5).
- **Heat and hot water:** Included in rent and paid by the landlord under the master lease (p. 5).
- **Water, sewer, trash, and Conservice fee:** The master lease bills these to residents; water and sewer are allocated by occupancy and square footage, trash is a flat monthly charge, and the billing-service fee is $3.95 monthly (p. 5). Before signing, the parties must write down how the subtenant will reimburse the sublessor for charges attributable to this occupancy, including how bills received after move-out will be handled. The sublessor will provide the bill or allocation basis.
- **Internet/cable:** Tenant-paid through a provider of the tenant’s choice under the master lease (p. 5). The parties must record before signing whether this service will be provided and how its cost will be shared.

## 5. Master lease rules carried down
The subtenant agrees to follow the applicable master lease terms and building rules, including:
- Use the premises as a residence and keep occupied areas clean and safe; use fixtures and appliances reasonably and do not damage the premises (CT-47a-11; master lease p. 1).
- No animals, even temporarily, without written authorization; assistance-animal requests follow the owner’s accommodation process (master lease p. 1).
- No guest may stay more than 7 consecutive days, or more than twice that many days in a month, without the landlord’s prior written consent; the resident is responsible for guest conduct and damage (master lease p. 1).
- Maintain personal liability insurance of at least $100,000 per occurrence and provide proof before move-in, with the owner listed as an interested party, as required by the master lease (p. 6). Confirm with the landlord what proof is acceptable for a subtenant.
- Submit repair requests through the online resident portal or deliver a signed written request to the office; emergency maintenance is available 24 hours (master lease p. 1).
- Observe the master lease’s utility payment rules and applicable due dates (p. 5).

## 6. Condition, hand-off, and return inspections
At hand-off, the parties will inspect together, complete a dated condition report, photograph existing conditions, record meter/account information if available, and exchange keys/access devices. The subtenant should report defects promptly in writing. The master lease requires an inventory form within 48 hours after move-in (p. 1); the parties will coordinate with the landlord so the subtenant can comply where applicable.

The parties will schedule a joint return inspection on or near July 28, 2027. They will record the condition, take dated photographs, document cleaning and key return, and give Rentrail escrow the inspection record. The subtenant will provide a forwarding address in writing. The sublessor will provide copies of invoices or other support for any proposed deduction and the required itemized accounting.

## 7. Responsibility and deductions
The subtenant is responsible for rent and agreed utility amounts for the sublease term, and for actual damage caused by the subtenant or the subtenant’s guests beyond ordinary wear and tear. No deduction will be proposed for a pre-existing condition or ordinary wear. Any deduction must be reasonable, itemized, supported, and consistent with Connecticut deposit law (CT-47a-21-d2; DOB-itemize). Disputes about deductions should be discussed promptly; undisputed funds should not be held back because of a disputed item.

The sublessor remains responsible to the master landlord for the master lease obligations, including subtenant damage, and the lease says residents remain liable even when a sublet is approved (p. 1). This sublease does not release the sublessor from that responsibility.

## 8. Master lease controls; no extension
This sublease is subordinate to the master lease. If the terms conflict, the master lease and the landlord’s written consent control. This agreement does not extend the master lease beyond July 31, 2027, create a right to remain after July 28, 2027, or waive any landlord approval requirement.

## 9. Signatures
By signing, the parties confirm that all blanks and payment arrangements have been completed and that they will comply with the master lease and applicable law.

runs.result:
{"consent_letter_en": "[DATE]

To: [LANDLORD/PROPERTY MANAGER]
Re: Request for written consent to sublet [PREMISES ADDRESS]

Dear [LANDLORD/PROPERTY MANAGER],

I am Alex Kim, a resident under the lease for the premises. Under the lease’s subletting provision (p. 1), I request your prior written consent for Jordan Rivera to occupy the premises from June 1, 2027 through July 28, 2027, at a sublease rent of $1,950 per month, with a $1,500 security deposit held in Rentrail escrow until the return inspection.

Please confirm in writing whether you approve this sublet and identify any required approval documents. The lease states that a $150 administrative fee applies if consent is granted (p. 1). Please advise how and when to pay it. I understand that I and any remaining residents continue to be responsible for the lease obligations, including damage caused by a subtenant (p. 1).

This request does not seek to change or extend the master lease. Please also confirm any move-in procedures that Jordan Rivera must complete, including proof of the required liability insurance (p. 6).

Sincerely,

Alex Kim
[PHONE/EMAIL]", "agreement_md_en": "# Sublease Agreement (Draft — Subject to Landlord’s Written Consent)

**Do not sign or allow occupancy until the landlord gives prior written consent.** The master lease requires written consent for a sublet (p. 1).

## 1. Parties and premises
- **Sublessor:** Alex Kim
- **Subtenant:** Jordan Rivera
- **Premises:** [PREMISES ADDRESS]
- **Master landlord/property manager:** [LANDLORD/PROPERTY MANAGER]
- **Master lease:** Lease running August 1, 2026 through July 31, 2027.

## 2. Term and rent
The sublease term is **June 1, 2027 through July 28, 2027**, subject to written landlord consent. Rent is **$1,950 per month**. Before signing, the parties must put in writing the exact payment dates and any prorated amount for the partial July period; no prorated amount is assumed in this draft. The master lease requires rent to be paid in advance through the resident portal by the first of the month and does not accept cash (p. 1). The parties must confirm the permitted payment method and avoid any arrangement that conflicts with the master lease.

## 3. Security deposit and escrow
The subtenant will pay a **$1,500 security deposit** to **Rentrail escrow**, to be held until the return inspection. Before accepting the funds, the parties must confirm that the escrow arrangement satisfies Connecticut’s requirement that a landlord deposit the full security deposit in an escrow account at a financial institution (CT-47a-21-h1). The sublessor, as a tenant who sublets, is a landlord for deposit purposes (CT-47a-21-a7).

The sublessor will provide the required written notice identifying the amount held and the financial institution’s name and address within 30 days after receiving the deposit (CT-47a-21-h4). The sublessor will return the deposit balance and applicable accrued interest, with a written itemized statement for any lawful deductions, no later than **August 18, 2027**, unless the statutory forwarding-address rule makes a later date applicable (CT-47a-21-d2; CT-47a-21-i). Any claimed deduction must be for an actual, supportable loss and itemized; ordinary wear and tear is not a damage deduction. The parties will not charge for pre-existing conditions. Any deposit use must be limited to legally permitted obligations and documented amounts (CT-47a-21-a14; CT-47a-21-d2; DOB-itemize).

## 4. Utilities and services
- **Electricity:** The subtenant is responsible during the sublease term and must arrange the account before move-in if the utility provider permits. The master lease says residents open an account with Shoreline Electric (p. 5).
- **Heat and hot water:** Included in rent and paid by the landlord under the master lease (p. 5).
- **Water, sewer, trash, and Conservice fee:** The master lease bills these to residents; water and sewer are allocated by occupancy and square footage, trash is a flat monthly charge, and the billing-service fee is $3.95 monthly (p. 5). Before signing, the parties must write down how the subtenant will reimburse the sublessor for charges attributable to this occupancy, including how bills received after move-out will be handled. The sublessor will provide the bill or allocation basis.
- **Internet/cable:** Tenant-paid through a provider of the tenant’s choice under the master lease (p. 5). The parties must record before signing whether this service will be provided and how its cost will be shared.

## 5. Master lease rules carried down
The subtenant agrees to follow the applicable master lease terms and building rules, including:
- Use the premises as a residence and keep occupied areas clean and safe; use fixtures and appliances reasonably and do not damage the premises (CT-47a-11; master lease p. 1).
- No animals, even temporarily, without written authorization; assistance-animal requests follow the owner’s accommodation process (master lease p. 1).
- No guest may stay more than 7 consecutive days, or more than twice that many days in a month, without the landlord’s prior written consent; the resident is responsible for guest conduct and damage (master lease p. 1).
- Maintain personal liability insurance of at least $100,000 per occurrence and provide proof before move-in, with the owner listed as an interested party, as required by the master lease (p. 6). Confirm with the landlord what proof is acceptable for a subtenant.
- Submit repair requests through the online resident portal or deliver a signed written request to the office; emergency maintenance is available 24 hours (master lease p. 1).
- Observe the master lease’s utility payment rules and applicable due dates (p. 5).

## 6. Condition, hand-off, and return inspections
At hand-off, the parties will inspect together, complete a dated condition report, photograph existing conditions, record meter/account information if available, and exchange keys/access devices. The subtenant should report defects promptly in writing. The master lease requires an inventory form within 48 hours after move-in (p. 1); the parties will coordinate with the landlord so the subtenant can comply where applicable.

The parties will schedule a joint return inspection on or near July 28, 2027. They will record the condition, take dated photographs, document cleaning and key return, and give Rentrail escrow the inspection record. The subtenant will provide a forwarding address in writing. The sublessor will provide copies of invoices or other support for any proposed deduction and the required itemized accounting.

## 7. Responsibility and deductions
The subtenant is responsible for rent and agreed utility amounts for the sublease term, and for actual damage caused by the subtenant or the subtenant’s guests beyond ordinary wear and tear. No deduction will be proposed for a pre-existing condition or ordinary wear. Any deduction must be reasonable, itemized, supported, and consistent with Connecticut deposit law (CT-47a-21-d2; DOB-itemize). Disputes about deductions should be discussed promptly; undisputed funds should not be held back because of a disputed item.

The sublessor remains responsible to the master landlord for the master lease obligations, including subtenant damage, and the lease says residents remain liable even when a sublet is approved (p. 1). This sublease does not release the sublessor from that responsibility.

## 8. Master lease controls; no extension
This sublease is subordinate to the master lease. If the terms conflict, the master lease and the landlord’s written consent control. This agreement does not extend the master lease beyond July 31, 2027, create a right to remain after July 28, 2027, or waive any landlord approval requirement.

## 1. Parties and premises
- **Sublessor:** [PERSON_1]

## 2. Term and rent
The sublease term is **June 1, 2027 through July 28, 2027**, subject to written landlord consent. Rent is **$1,950 per month**. Before signing, the parties must put in writing the exact payment dates and any prorated amount for the partial July period; no prorated amount is assumed in this draft. The master lease requires rent to be paid in advance through the resident portal by the first of the month and does not accept cash (p. 1). The parties must confirm the permitted payment method and avoid any arrangement that conflicts with the master lease.

## 3. Security deposit and escrow
The subtenant will pay a **$1,500 security deposit** to **Rentrail escrow**, to be held until the return inspection. Before accepting the funds, the parties must confirm that the escrow arrangement satisfies Connecticut’s requirement that a landlord deposit the full security deposit in an escrow account at a financial institution (CT-47a-21-h1). The sublessor, as a tenant who sublets, is a landlord for deposit purposes (CT-47a-21-a7).

The sublessor will provide the required written notice identifying the amount held and the financial institution’s name and address within 30 days after receiving the deposit (CT-47a-21-h4). The sublessor will return the deposit balance and applicable accrued interest, with a written itemized statement for any lawful deductions, no later than **August 18, 2027**, unless the statutory forwarding-address rule makes a later date applicable (CT-47a-21-d2; CT-47a-21-i). Any claimed deduction must be for an actual, supportable loss and itemized; ordinary wear and tear is not a damage deduction. The parties will not charge for pre-existing conditions. Any deposit use must be limited to legally permitted obligations and documented amounts (CT-47a-21-a14; CT-47a-21-d2; DOB-itemize).

- **Electricity:** The subtenant is responsible during the sublease term and must arrange the account before move-in if the utility provider permits. The master lease says residents open an account with Shoreline Electric (p. 5).

Before signing, the parties must write down how the subtenant will reimburse the sublessor for charges attributable to this occupancy, including how bills received after move-out will be handled. - **Internet/cable:** Tenant-paid through a provider of the tenant’s choice under the master lease (p. 5). The parties must record before signing whether this service will be provided and how its cost will be shared.

The subtenant agrees to follow the applicable master lease terms and building rules, including:
- Use the premises as a residence and keep occupied areas clean and safe; use fixtures and appliances reasonably and do not damage the premises (CT-47a-11; master lease p. 1).
- No animals, even temporarily, without written authorization; assistance-animal requests follow the owner’s accommodation process (master lease p. 1).
- No guest may stay more than 7 consecutive days, or more than twice that many days in a month, without the landlord’s prior written consent; the resident is responsible for guest conduct and damage (master lease p. 1).
- Maintain personal liability insurance of at least $100,000 per occurrence and provide proof before move-in, with the owner listed as an interested party, as required by the master lease (p. 6). Confirm with the landlord what proof is acceptable for a subtenant.
- Submit repair requests through the online resident portal or deliver a signed written request to the office; emergency maintenance is available 24 hours (master lease p. 1).
- Observe the master lease’s utility payment rules and applicable due dates (p. 5).

## 6. Condition, hand-off, and return inspections
At hand-off, the parties will inspect together, complete a dated condition report, photograph existing conditions, record meter/account information if available, and exchange keys/access devices. The subtenant should report defects promptly in writing. The master lease requires an inventory form within 48 hours after move-in (p. 1); the parties will coordinate with the landlord so the subtenant can comply where applicable.

The parties will schedule a joint return inspection on or near July 28, 2027. They will record the condition, take dated photographs, document cleaning and key return, and give Rentrail escrow the inspection record. The subtenant will provide a forwarding address in writing. The sublessor will provide copies of invoices or other support for any proposed deduction and the required itemized accounting.

## 7. Responsibility and deductions
The subtenant is responsible for rent and agreed utility amounts for the sublease term, and for actual damage caused by the subtenant or the subtenant’s guests beyond ordinary wear and tear. No deduction will be proposed for a pre-existing condition or ordinary wear. Any deduction must be reasonable, itemized, supported, and consistent with Connecticut deposit law (CT-47a-21-d2; DOB-itemize). Disputes about deductions should be discussed promptly; undisputed funds should not be held back because of a disputed item.

The sublessor remains responsible to the master landlord for the master lease obligations, including subtenant damage, and the lease says residents remain liable even when a sublet is approved (p. 1). This sublease does not release the sublessor from that responsibility.

## 8. Master lease controls; no extension
This sublease is subordinate to the master lease. If the terms conflict, the master lease and the landlord’s written consent control. This agreement does not extend the master lease beyond July 31, 2027, create a right to remain after July 28, 2027, or waive any landlord approval requirement.

posts.title: Can my landlord charge carpet cleaning "regardless of condition" in CT?
posts.body: My lease says professional carpet cleaning regardless of condition. The carpet was fine when I left. Can they deduct it?

comments.body:
Yes. A tenant who sublets is treated as a landlord, so the Connecticut deposit-interest rules apply. Interest accrues at the 2026 rate of 0.49% per year; if your sublet ended before the tenancy anniversary, accrued interest is due within 21 days after it ended. You generally lose interest for any month you were over 10 days late on rent, unless the landlord charged a late fee. The exact amount depends on how long the $1,500 was held.

Sources: CT-47a-21-a7, CT-47a-21-i, CT-47a-21-d2

A “regardless of condition” clause does not by itself make a carpet-cleaning deduction valid. Connecticut allows a deposit deduction for actual damages caused by your failure to meet tenant obligations; those include keeping the premises as clean as their condition permits. If the carpet was left clean and the landlord cannot show an actual cleaning-related failure or damage, the charge is contestable. Ask for an itemized explanation and evidence; a local tenant-rights group or lawyer can confirm if disputed.

Sources: CT-47a-21-a14, CT-47a-21-d2, CT-47a-11
